title: Record Video with a Teleprompter on iPhone & iPad
description: Record with scrolling scripts or swipeable cue cards in CueCard. Save to Photos, compare Takes and keep your words out of the video.
body:
## From script to finished take

Write and save a script, open the teleprompter, then tap the camera. CueCard puts a movable camera window beside your words so you can check the frame while you read. Your script stays out of the camera footage. You can also record with swipeable cue cards when you prefer prompts to a full script.

Pause when you need another moment, resume the take, and stop to save it to Photos. With synchronized controls enabled, teleprompter playback and recording start and pause together. [Follow the recording steps](/help/recording-video/).

## Review without losing your script

Open Takes from the reading view or Library. Watch a take, add notes about what worked, tag it, or favorite the best version. Favorites and albums connect to Photos. **Deleting a take also deletes it from Photos.** [Learn how Takes works](/help/takes/).

Try three takes of the same short opening. Change just one thing each time: your pace, where you pause, or how close the text sits to the lens. Keep the one that sounds like you.

## Set up the camera for the job

Choose resolution, frame rate, dynamic range, codec, stabilization and front-camera mirroring in Settings. Available combinations depend on the device and selected camera; changes made while recording apply to the next take. [Choose camera settings](/help/camera-settings/).

## Already have a favorite recording app?

Close CueCard’s camera and float the teleprompter over another app instead. Use this when you need that app’s recording workflow. Test a short clip first: camera and audio behavior varies between apps. Phone screen recording can capture the floating script; camera video does not. [Set up the floating window](/help/floating-window/).

## Start with something worth saying

Use a [free teleprompter script](/teleprompter-scripts/) or a [cue-card template](/cue-card-templates/). CueCard is free on iPhone and iPad, with no ads, subscription or required account.
heading: Your script. Your camera. One app.

title: Voice-Following Teleprompter for iPhone | CueCard
description: Follow Me AI beta moves your script as you read aloud. Learn how it differs from fixed-speed scrolling and check its requirements.
body:
## Let your spoken words set the pace

Follow Me AI (Beta) listens as you read and moves the teleprompter through your script. It is useful when a fixed scroll speed makes you rush or leaves you waiting for the next line. The timer starts with your first words.

Open the teleprompter and tap the waveform for each session. Pause stops listening; Play listens again. [Set up Follow Me AI](/help/voice-following/).

## On-device speech, with clear limits

Voice recognition runs on the device. It needs microphone and speech-recognition permission, plus on-device recognition support for your script’s language. Background voices, unusual names and departures from the written script can affect tracking. Rehearse before an important recording.

This beta uses speech recognition. Suggestions AI and Help AI use an Apple Intelligence model and have separate availability requirements. The [setup and troubleshooting guide](/help/voice-following/) explains what to do when a control or language is unavailable.

## Choose the mode that fits the session

Use voice-following when you want to vary your pace while staying close to the script. Use fixed-speed scrolling when you want a predictable pace without microphone recognition, or when speech support is unavailable. You can always pause, drag the script or use anchors to get back to your place.

Try this line at two different speeds: “Here is the idea. [pause] Give it a moment. Now show the example.” The cue is a reminder to pause yourself, not an automatic playback command. [Compare voice-following and fixed speed](/blog/voice-following-vs-fixed-speed/).
heading: A teleprompter that follows your voice.

title: iPhone & iPad Teleprompter for Mirror Glass | CueCard
description: Flip your script horizontally or vertically for teleprompter glass, set a comfortable reading line and control playback from Apple Watch.
body:
## Put your script behind the glass

Use CueCard on an iPhone or iPad as the text display in a teleprompter rig. In **Settings → Teleprompter**, turn on **Flip Horizontally** or **Flip Vertically** to suit the way your screen reflects through the glass. These settings also apply to the floating window.

## Check orientation before a full script

1. Write a short test line with a word that is easy to recognize, such as “Camera ready.”
2. Place your device in the rig and look through the glass from your speaking position.
3. If the reflected words read backward, adjust horizontal flipping. If the orientation is upside down, check device orientation and vertical flipping.
4. Set text size and reading speed while standing where you will actually speak.

Glass placement and rig orientation differ. Judge the reflected words, then run a short camera test to check the eyeline. [Read the mirroring help](/help/mirror-and-reading-guide/).

## Keep your place without reaching for the screen

Drag the reading-guide pointer to a comfortable line. Add anchors at the start of major sections so you can jump back when rehearsing. With the Apple Watch app, you can play, pause and go back ten seconds on the phone teleprompter. [Set up Watch controls](/help/cards-and-watch/).

## Text flipping is separate from camera mirroring

**Flip Horizontally** and **Flip Vertically** change the script display. **Mirror Front Camera** changes the saved video from CueCard’s front camera. Configure each for its own purpose; changing one does not fix the other.

Use a separate camera for your rig, or explore [recording in CueCard](/record-video/) for a phone-based setup. The app does not include physical teleprompter hardware.
heading: Your words, reflected right.
